<td style="background:#DEC240; padding: 10px; border-radius: 40px; -moz-border-radius: 40px; -webkit-border-radius: 40px; -khtml-border-radius: 40px; -icab-border-radius: 40px; -o-border-radius: 40px;" align="center"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:0013Weedle.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/3/36/0013Weedle.png/50px-0013Weedle.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="50" height="50" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/3/36/0013Weedle.png/75px-0013Weedle.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/3/36/0013Weedle.png/100px-0013Weedle.png 2x" data-file-width="1023" data-file-height="1023"></a></span>

<td style="padding-left:3px; padding-right:20px">This page is in need of <a href="/wiki/Bulbapedia:Spading" title="Bulbapedia:Spading">spading</a>. See its section on the spading page for more information, and how you can help.<br><small>Reason: Formula in Generation V onward, if different</small>

<dl><dd><i>This article is about the game mechanic. For the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Adventures" title="Pokémon Adventures">Pokémon Adventures</a> chapter whose Japanese title translates to "Escape!!", see <a href="/wiki/PS268" title="PS268">PS268</a>.</i> <i>For the Escape Orb in the Mystery Dungeon series, see <a href="/wiki/Wonder_Orb" title="Wonder Orb">Wonder Orb</a>.</i></dd></dl>
<hr>
<figure typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:Smoke_Ball_escape_III.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/3/3c/Smoke_Ball_escape_III.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="240" height="160" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="240" data-file-height="160"></a><figcaption>Escaping via <a href="/wiki/Smoke_Ball" title="Smoke Ball">Smoke Ball</a> in Generation III.</figcaption></figure>
<p>In the <a href="/wiki/Core_series" title="Core series">core series</a> Pokémon games, it is possible to <b>escape</b> (Japanese: <b><span class="explain" title="に">逃</span>げる</b> <i>escape</i>) from a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_battle" title="Pokémon battle">battle</a> with a <a href="/wiki/Wild_Pok%C3%A9mon" title="Wild Pokémon">wild Pokémon</a> by selecting <b>Run</b> (Japanese: <b>にげる</b> <i>Run</i>) on the main battle screen. However, escape is not guaranteed; whether the player is successful at running away from the battle is determined by a calculation involving the speed of the combatants. When the escape is successful, the battle ends immediately. When it is not successful, the wild Pokémon will use a move.
</p><p>Entering a battle with a wild Pokémon and then escaping counts the Pokémon as being seen in the Trainer's <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9dex" title="Pokédex">Pokédex</a>. In <a href="/wiki/Generation" title="Generation">Generations</a> <a href="/wiki/Generation_I" title="Generation I">I</a> and <a href="/wiki/Generation_II" title="Generation II">II</a>, if the player runs from an <a href="/wiki/List_of_wild_Pok%C3%A9mon_from_in-game_events" title="List of wild Pokémon from in-game events">in-game event Pokémon</a>, it becomes permanently unavailable (except the <a href="/wiki/Electrode_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Electrode (Pokémon)">Electrode</a> in <a href="/wiki/Team_Rocket_HQ" title="Team Rocket HQ">Team Rocket HQ</a>). Starting in <a href="/wiki/Generation_III" title="Generation III">Generation III</a>, if the player runs from a <a href="/wiki/Legendary_Pok%C3%A9mon" title="Legendary Pokémon">Legendary Pokémon</a>, the Pokémon reappears when the player leaves and re-enters its location.
</p>

<table align="center" style="margin: 3px auto; background: rgb(250, 255, 244); border: 2px solid rgb(175, 169, 129); border-radius: 40px;">

<tbody><tr>
<td style="background:#CBC7AD; padding: 10px; border-radius: 40px; -moz-border-radius: 40px; -webkit-border-radius: 40px; -khtml-border-radius: 40px; -icab-border-radius: 40px; -o-border-radius: 40px;;" width="50px" align="center"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:0140Kabuto.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/d/d2/0140Kabuto.png/50px-0140Kabuto.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="50" height="50" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/d/d2/0140Kabuto.png/75px-0140Kabuto.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/d/d2/0140Kabuto.png/100px-0140Kabuto.png 2x" data-file-width="500" data-file-height="500"></a></span>
</td>
<td style="padding-left:3px; padding-right:20px"><b>This section contains old or outdated information, or has not been updated in a while.</b><br>Please check the content of this section and update it as required. <br><small>Reason: everything after Generation 4.</small>
</td></tr></tbody></table> 
<p>Generally speaking, the slower the Trainer's Pokémon and/or the faster the wild Pokémon, the harder it is to escape.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Generation_I_and_II">Generation I and II</span></h3>
<p>If the player's active Pokémon's Speed is greater than or equal to the wild Pokémon's Speed, fleeing will always succeed. Otherwise, under normal circumstances, the chance of escaping is determined by the following formula
<math class="mwe-math-element" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mi>O</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>E</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>P</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mo lspace="0.27777777777778em" rspace="0.27777777777778em">mod</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>s</mi></mstyle></mrow></math>
where
</p>
<ul><li><code>Speed<sub>Player</sub></code> is the current <a href="/wiki/Stat#Speed" title="Stat">Speed</a> of the player's active Pokémon,</li>
<li><code>Speed<sub>Wild</sub></code> is the Speed of the wild Pokémon, and</li>
<li><code>Attempts</code> is the number of consecutive times the player has tried to escape during the battle (counting the current attempt). If the player's Pokémon attacks, this number is reset to 0.</li></ul>
<p>If <code>Odds<sub>Escape</sub></code> is greater than 255, the player escapes automatically. Otherwise, a random number is generated between 0 and 255. If that number is less than <code>Odds<sub>Escape</sub></code>, the player escapes. If not, the escape fails and the player's Pokémon does not make a move that turn. If <math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mo lspace="0.27777777777778em" rspace="0.27777777777778em">mod</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace></mrow></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> is equal to 0, escape is automatically a success.
</p><p>In those generations, the speed drop from <a href="/wiki/Paralysis_(status_condition)" title="Paralysis (status condition)">paralysis</a> affects the chance of escaping.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Generation_III_and_IV">Generation III and IV</span></h3>
<p>If the player's active Pokémon's Speed is greater than or equal to the wild Pokémon's Speed, fleeing will always succeed. Otherwise, the chance of successfully fleeing is determined by the following formula:
<math class="mwe-math-element" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mi>O</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>E</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">(</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>P</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn><mn>8</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>s</mi><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">)</mo></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mo lspace="0.27777777777778em" rspace="0.27777777777778em">mod</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace></mrow></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math>
where 
</p>
<ul><li><code>Speed<sub>Player</sub></code> is the unmodified <a href="/wiki/Stat#Speed" title="Stat">Speed</a> of the player's active Pokémon,</li>
<li><code>Speed<sub>Wild</sub></code> is the unmodified Speed of the wild Pokémon,</li>
<li><code>Attempts</code> is the number of times the player has tried to escape during the battle (counting the current attempt).</li></ul>
<p>A random number is generated between 0 and 255. If that number is less than <code>Odds<sub>Escape</sub></code>, the player escapes. If not, the escape fails and the player's Pokémon does not make a move that turn.
</p><p>From Generation III onwards, the speed drop from <a href="/wiki/Paralysis_(status_condition)" title="Paralysis (status condition)">paralysis</a> no longer affects the chance of escaping.
</p>
<div id="AdThrive_Content_1_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-1 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px; align-content: start;" data-google-query-id="CNyrmczG9pYDFTjySQUd_TA2ag"><div id="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0__container__" style="border: 0pt;"><iframe id="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0" name="google_ads_iframe_/18190176,1027503/AdThrive_Content_1/630428a76245162875c78210_0" title="3rd party ad content" width="1" height="1" scrolling="no" marginwidth="0" marginheight="0" frameborder="0" aria-label="Advertisement" tabindex="0" allow="private-state-token-redemption" data-load-complete="true" data-google-container-id="2" style="border: 0px; vertical-align: bottom;"></iframe></div></div><h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Generation_V_onwards">Generation V onwards</span></h3>
<p>If the player's active Pokémon's Speed is greater than or equal to the wild Pokémon's Speed, fleeing will always succeed. Otherwise, the chance of successfully fleeing is determined by the following formula:
</p>
<dl><dd><math class="mwe-math-element" display="block" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mi>O</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>E</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>P</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>y</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>r</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>s</mi></mstyle></mrow></math></dd></dl>
<p>where
</p>
<ul><li><code>Speed<sub>Player</sub></code> is the unmodified <a href="/wiki/Stat#Speed" title="Stat">Speed</a> of the player's active Pokémon,</li>
<li><code>Speed<sub>Wild</sub></code> is the unmodified Speed of the wild Pokémon,</li>
<li><code>Attempts</code> is the number of times the player has tried to escape during the battle (counting the current attempt).</li></ul>
<p>A random number is generated between 0 and 255. If that number is less than <code>Odds<sub>Escape</sub></code>, the player escapes. If not, the escape fails and the player's Pokémon does not make a move that turn.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Other_factors">Other factors</span></h3>
<table align="center" style="margin: 3px auto; background: rgb(250, 255, 244); border: 2px solid rgb(145, 81, 33); border-radius: 40px;">

<tbody><tr>
<td style="background:#B88E6F; padding: 10px; border-radius: 40px; -moz-border-radius: 40px; -webkit-border-radius: 40px; -khtml-border-radius: 40px; -icab-border-radius: 40px; -o-border-radius: 40px;;" width="50px" align="center"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:0050Diglett.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/50px-0050Diglett.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="50" height="50" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/75px-0050Diglett.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/100px-0050Diglett.png 2x" data-file-width="758" data-file-height="758"></a></span>
</td>
<td style="padding-left:3px; padding-right:20px"><b>This section is incomplete.</b><br>Please feel free to edit this section to add missing information and complete it. <br><small>Reason: <br>* In Generation II, if a Pokémon holding a Smoke Ball faints and the player chooses to flee, is the player guaranteed to escape?<br>* Exact Battle Pyramid mechanics.</small>
</td></tr></tbody></table> 
<p>Pokémon cannot attempt to flee from Trainer battles or battles during <a href="/wiki/Island_challenge" title="Island challenge">trials</a>. In the <a href="/wiki/Generation_II" title="Generation II">Generation II</a> games only, the player cannot attempt to flee from Pokémon encountered as traps in the <a href="/wiki/Team_Rocket_HQ" title="Team Rocket HQ">Team Rocket's Hideout</a>, the <a href="/wiki/GS_Ball" title="GS Ball">GS Ball</a> <a href="/wiki/Celebi_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Celebi (Pokémon)">Celebi</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Bell_Tower" title="Bell Tower">Tin Tower</a> <a href="/wiki/Suicune_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Suicune (Pokémon)">Suicune</a> (in Crystal), and the scripted <a href="/wiki/Red_Gyarados" title="Red Gyarados">Red Gyarados</a>. In the <a href="/wiki/Battle_Pyramid" title="Battle Pyramid">Battle Pyramid</a>, escape is not guaranteed if the player's Pokémon is faster.
</p><p>Several conditions prevent a Pokémon from even attempting to flee.
</p>
<ul><li>A Pokémon with the Ability <a href="/wiki/Shadow_Tag_(Ability)" title="Shadow Tag (Ability)">Shadow Tag</a> prevents opposing Pokémon from attempting to flee. (From Generation IV onward, Pokémon with Shadow Tag are unaffected by Shadow Tag.)</li>
<li>A Pokémon with the Ability <a href="/wiki/Arena_Trap_(Ability)" title="Arena Trap (Ability)">Arena Trap</a> prevents opposing <a href="/wiki/Grounded" title="Grounded">grounded</a> Pokémon from attempting to flee.</li>
<li>A Pokémon with the Ability <a href="/wiki/Magnet_Pull_(Ability)" title="Magnet Pull (Ability)">Magnet Pull</a> prevents opposing <a href="/wiki/Steel_(type)" title="Steel (type)">Steel-type</a> Pokémon from attempting to flee.</li>
<li>A Pokémon affected by a <a href="/wiki/Category:Trapping_moves" title="Category:Trapping moves">trapping move</a> (including <a href="/wiki/Category:Binding_moves" title="Category:Binding moves">binding moves</a> and <a href="/wiki/Ingrain_(move)" title="Ingrain (move)">Ingrain</a>) is prevented from attempting to flee (from Generation II onward).</li></ul>
<p>Several conditions allow a Pokémon to always successfully flee from a wild battle.
</p>
<ul><li>Using an <a href="/wiki/Escape_item" title="Escape item">escape item</a> (<a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Doll" title="Poké Doll">Poké Doll</a>, <a href="/wiki/Fluffy_Tail" title="Fluffy Tail">Fluffy Tail</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Toy" title="Poké Toy">Poké Toy</a>) causes the player to escape from a wild Pokémon (regardless of trapping moves and Abilities).</li>
<li>In a wild Single Battle (including an <a href="/wiki/SOS_Battle" title="SOS Battle">SOS Battle</a> as long as there is currently only a single opponent), using the move <a href="/wiki/Teleport_(move)" title="Teleport (move)">Teleport</a> causes the Pokémon to flee, unless a trapping move or Ability prevents escape. From Generation V onward, <a href="/wiki/Ingrain_(move)" title="Ingrain (move)">Ingrain</a> does not prevent Teleport from being successful.</li>
<li>If the player's Pokémon is holding a <a href="/wiki/Smoke_Ball" title="Smoke Ball">Smoke Ball</a> or has the Ability <a href="/wiki/Run_Away_(Ability)" title="Run Away (Ability)">Run Away</a>, its attempts to flee or Teleport are always successful (regardless of trapping moves and Abilities). In Generation II only, the Smoke Ball doesn't guarantee escape if a trapping move would prevent it.
<ul><li>In the <a href="/wiki/Battle_Pyramid" title="Battle Pyramid">Battle Pyramid</a>, Run Away does not guarantee escape, but it will be credited if a Pokémon with this Ability successfully flees.</li>
<li>In Generation III and IV, if the player's Pokémon that has Run Away or a Smoke Ball faints, if the player attempts to flee instead of sending out another Pokémon, they will escape without fail.</li>
<li>In Generation III only, the Smoke Ball has an animation when escaping using it. In Generation II, "Got away safely" redundantly appears after the message informing of escape via Smoke Ball.</li>
<li>In Generation V only, a wild Pokémon holding a Smoke Ball cannot successfully Teleport if it is trapped by a trapping move or Ability (although the player's Pokémon can).</li></ul></li>
<li>From <a href="/wiki/Generation_VI" title="Generation VI">Generation VI</a> onward, the player's <a href="/wiki/Ghost_(type)" title="Ghost (type)">Ghost-type</a> Pokémon can always successfully flee, regardless of trapping moves or Abilities.</li></ul>
<p>In a wild Single Battle (including an <a href="/wiki/SOS_Battle" title="SOS Battle">SOS Battle</a> as long as there is currently only a single opponent), the moves <a href="/wiki/Whirlwind_(move)" title="Whirlwind (move)">Whirlwind</a>, <a href="/wiki/Roar_(move)" title="Roar (move)">Roar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dragon_Tail_(move)" title="Dragon Tail (move)">Dragon Tail</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Circle_Throw_(move)" title="Circle Throw (move)">Circle Throw</a> force the target to flee, unless it has the Ability <a href="/wiki/Suction_Cups_(Ability)" title="Suction Cups (Ability)">Suction Cups</a> or has been affected by <a href="/wiki/Ingrain_(move)" title="Ingrain (move)">Ingrain</a>. If a wild Pokémon's held <a href="/wiki/Red_Card" title="Red Card">Red Card</a> is activated while it has no allies, it forces the player's Pokémon to flee.
</p><p>In a wild battle, the Abilities <a href="/wiki/Wimp_Out_(Ability)" title="Wimp Out (Ability)">Wimp Out</a> and <a href="/wiki/Emergency_Exit_(Ability)" title="Emergency Exit (Ability)">Emergency Exit</a> cause the Pokémon with that Ability to flee if its HP falls below half.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Example">Example</span></h3>
<div id="AdThrive_Content_2_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-2 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Generation_I_and_II_2">Generation I and II</span></h4>
<p>The player's Pokémon has a Speed of 25 and the wild Pokémon has a Speed of 100. The player tries to escape, and has not previously attempted to flee in the battle.
</p><p>First, check that the denominator <math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>S</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>e</mi><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>W</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>l</mi><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mo lspace="0.27777777777778em" rspace="0.27777777777778em">mod</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace></mrow></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math> will not be equal to 0
</p><p><math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mtable columnalign="right left right left right left right left right left right left" columnspacing="0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="3pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>D</mi><mi>e</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>m</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>r</mi></mtd><mtd><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mo lspace="0.27777777777778em" rspace="0.27777777777778em">mod</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">⌊</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">⌋</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mo lspace="0.27777777777778em" rspace="0.27777777777778em">mod</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mo lspace="0.27777777777778em" rspace="0.27777777777778em">mod</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mspace width="0.167em"></mspace></mrow></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math>
</p><p>Since the denominator is not equal to 0, proceed to calculating the odds of escape.
</p><p><math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mtable columnalign="right left right left right left right left right left right left" columnspacing="0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em 2em 0em" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="3pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>O</mi><mi>d</mi><mi>d</mi><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mi>E</mi><mi>s</mi><mi>c</mi><mi>a</mi><mi>p</mi><mi>e</mi></mrow></mrow></msub></mtd><mtd><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="true" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"><mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">⌊</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn><mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">⌋</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">+</mo><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><mo stretchy="false">=</mo><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mstyle></mrow></math>
</p><p>Since <code>Odds<sub>Escape</sub></code> is not greater than 255, generate a random number between 0 and 255. If that random number is less than 62, the Pokémon flees successfully. Therefore, the probability of escaping is <math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow><mo stretchy="false">≈</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mstyle></mrow></math>.
</p><p>If the player fails to escape, each successive attempt will be <math class="mwe-math-element" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mstyle displaystyle="false" scriptlevel="0"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mfrac><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>3</mn><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"><mn>2</mn><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mstyle></mrow><mo stretchy="false">≈</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">.</mo><mn>7</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">%</mi></mstyle></mrow></math> more likely than the last.
</p>
<h2><span id="Wild_Pok.C3.A9mon"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Wild_Pokémon">Wild Pokémon</span></h2>
<p>Certain wild Pokémon can flee from battle.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Safari_Zone">Safari Zone</span></h3>
<p>In Generation I, III, and IV, as well as <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Brilliant_Diamond_and_Shining_Pearl" title="Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl">Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl</a>, Pokémon encountered during a <a href="/wiki/Safari_Game" class="mw-redirect" title="Safari Game">Safari Game</a> in a <a href="/wiki/Safari_Zone" title="Safari Zone">Safari Zone</a> can flee. The rate of escape can be affected by throwing Bait, <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9block" title="Pokéblock">Pokéblocks</a>, Rocks, or Mud or by "going near" (depending on the game). Usually food lowers the chance to flee while also lowering the <a href="/wiki/Catch_rate" title="Catch rate">catch rate</a>, and other actions increase the chance to flee while increasing the catch rate; but the Great Marsh switches those effects.
</p>
<ul><li><b><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Red_and_Blue_Versions" title="Pokémon Red and Blue Versions"><span style="color:#DA3914;">R</span><span style="color:#2E50D8;">B</span></a><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Yellow_Version" title="Pokémon Yellow Version"><span style="color:#FFD733;">Y</span></a></b>: in the <a href="/wiki/Kanto_Safari_Zone" title="Kanto Safari Zone">Kanto Safari Zone</a>, the chance a Pokémon will flee is based on its <a href="/wiki/Stat#Speed" title="Stat">Speed</a>; throwing Bait lowers this chance, while throwing Rocks raises it.</li>
<li><b><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ruby_and_Sapphire_Versions" title="Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire Versions"><span style="color:#CD2236;">R</span><span style="color:#3D51A7;">S</span></a><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Emerald_Version" title="Pokémon Emerald Version"><span style="color:#009652;">E</span></a></b>: in the <a href="/wiki/Hoenn_Safari_Zone" title="Hoenn Safari Zone">Hoenn Safari Zone</a>, all Pokémon start with the same flee rate; throwing a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9block" title="Pokéblock">Pokéblock</a> lowers this rate, while going nearer to the Pokémon raises it.</li>
<li><b><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_FireRed_and_LeafGreen_Versions" title="Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen Versions"><span style="color:#F15C01;">FR</span><span style="color:#9FDC00;">LG</span></a></b>: in the <a href="/wiki/Kanto_Safari_Zone" title="Kanto Safari Zone">Kanto Safari Zone</a>, each species has <a href="/wiki/Kanto_Safari_Zone#Generation_III" title="Kanto Safari Zone">its own flee rate</a> and this is influenced by whether the Pokémon is eating (lower) or angry (higher).</li>
<li><b><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Diamond_and_Pearl_Versions" title="Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Versions"><span style="color:#90BEED;">D</span><span style="color:#DD7CB1;">P</span></a><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Platinum_Version" title="Pokémon Platinum Version"><span style="color:#A0A08D;">Pt</span></a></b>: in the <a href="/wiki/Great_Marsh" title="Great Marsh">Great Marsh</a>, each species has <a href="/wiki/Great_Marsh#Base_flee_rates" title="Great Marsh">its own flee rate</a>; throwing Mud lowers this rate, while throwing Bait has a high chance of raising it.</li>
<li><b><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_HeartGold_and_SoulSilver_Versions" title="Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver Versions"><span style="color:#E8B502;">HG</span><span style="color:#6F7887;">SS</span></a></b>:in the <a href="/wiki/Johto_Safari_Zone" title="Johto Safari Zone">Johto Safari Zone</a>, each species has <a href="/wiki/Johto_Safari_Zone#Base_flee_rates" title="Johto Safari Zone">its own flee rate</a>; throwing Bait lowers this rate, while throwing Mud has a high chance of raising it.</li>
<li><b><a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Brilliant_Diamond_and_Shining_Pearl" title="Pokémon Brilliant Diamond and Shining Pearl"><span style="color:#44BAE5;">BD</span><span style="color:#DA7D99;">SP</span></a></b>: in the <a href="/wiki/Great_Marsh" title="Great Marsh">Great Marsh</a>, each species has <a href="/wiki/Great_Marsh#Base_flee_rates" title="Great Marsh">its own flee rate</a>; throwing Mud lowers this rate, while throwing Bait raises it.</li></ul>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Generation_II">Generation II</span></h3>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Gold_and_Silver_Versions" title="Pokémon Gold and Silver Versions">Pokémon Gold, Silver</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Crystal_Version" title="Pokémon Crystal Version">Crystal</a>, in addition to the <a href="/wiki/Roaming_Pok%C3%A9mon" title="Roaming Pokémon">roaming</a> <a href="/wiki/Legendary_beasts" title="Legendary beasts">Legendary beasts</a>, a few species of wild Pokémon can escape from battle. Much like <a href="/wiki/Roaming_Pok%C3%A9mon" title="Roaming Pokémon">roaming Pokémon</a>, these Pokémon may attempt to flee immediately before they would use their move, and they will not attempt to flee when affected by <a href="/wiki/Category:Trapping_moves" title="Category:Trapping moves">trapping moves</a> (such as <a href="/wiki/Mean_Look_(move)" title="Mean Look (move)">Mean Look</a> or <a href="/wiki/Wrap_(move)" title="Wrap (move)">Wrap</a>), <a href="/wiki/Sleep_(status_condition)" title="Sleep (status condition)">sleep</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Freeze_(status_condition)" title="Freeze (status condition)">freeze</a>.
</p><p>All Pokémon that can flee were intended to be more likely to be caught in a <a href="/wiki/Fast_Ball" title="Fast Ball">Fast Ball</a>, but due to a programming error, only <a href="/wiki/Magnemite_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Magnemite (Pokémon)">Magnemite</a>, <a href="/wiki/Grimer_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Grimer (Pokémon)">Grimer</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Tangela_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Tangela (Pokémon)">Tangela</a> actually are more likely to be caught in a Fast Ball.

<div id="AdThrive_Content_3_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-3 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h3><span id="Roaming_Pok.C3.A9mon"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Roaming_Pokémon">Roaming Pokémon</span></h3>
<p><a href="/wiki/Roaming_Pok%C3%A9mon" title="Roaming Pokémon">Roaming Pokémon</a> attempt to flee every turn, unless they are prevented from fleeing (such as by <a href="/wiki/Category:Trapping_moves" title="Category:Trapping moves">trapping moves</a>).
</p><p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_X_and_Y" title="Pokémon X and Y">Pokémon X and Y</a>, roaming <a href="/wiki/Articuno_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Articuno (Pokémon)">Articuno</a>, <a href="/wiki/Zapdos_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Zapdos (Pokémon)">Zapdos</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Moltres_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Moltres (Pokémon)">Moltres</a> will automatically flee before even the first turn. The player must encounter the Legendary Pokémon ten times before finally battling it in <a href="/wiki/Sea_Spirit%27s_Den" title="Sea Spirit's Den">Sea Spirit's Den</a>.
</p>
<h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon:_Let.27s_Go.2C_Pikachu.21_and_Let.27s_Go.2C_Eevee.21"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon:_Let's_Go,_Pikachu!_and_Let's_Go,_Eevee!">Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!</span></h3>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon:_Let%27s_Go,_Pikachu!_and_Let%27s_Go,_Eevee!" title="Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!">Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!</a>, the capture mechanics are similar to that of <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO" title="Pokémon GO">Pokémon GO</a>. Wild Pokémon excluding <a href="/wiki/Legendary_Pok%C3%A9mon" title="Legendary Pokémon">Legendary Pokémon</a> have a chance of fleeing during an encounter after breaking out of a Poké Ball. If the player has a <a href="/wiki/Catch_Combo" title="Catch Combo">Catch Combo</a>, a wild Pokémon fleeing will cause it to be lost, but the player fleeing from a wild Pokémon will not. Shortly before fleeing, an animation different to the one when a wild Pokémon swats a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Ball" title="Poké Ball">Poké Ball</a> away will play. After this animation has played any thrown Poké Balls (except the <a href="/wiki/Master_Ball" title="Master Ball">Master Ball</a>) will fail to catch it and it will flee.
</p><p>Every time a Pokémon can flee, the game rolls a value from 0 to 255 and compares it to the current flee value; if it is higher, the Pokémon escapes. This value starts at 242 (minus twice the current Catch Combo) and decreases for any throw that isn't Excellent (5 for Great, 10 for Nice and 20 for generic); a missed throw does not change the value.<sup id="cite_ref-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-2"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>2<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p><p><br>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Other">Other</span></h3>
<table align="center" style="margin: 3px auto; background: rgb(250, 255, 244); border: 2px solid rgb(145, 81, 33); border-radius: 40px;">

<tbody><tr>
<td style="background:#B88E6F; padding: 10px; border-radius: 40px; -moz-border-radius: 40px; -webkit-border-radius: 40px; -khtml-border-radius: 40px; -icab-border-radius: 40px; -o-border-radius: 40px;;" width="50px" align="center"><span typeof="mw:File"><a href="/wiki/File:0050Diglett.png" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/50px-0050Diglett.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="50" height="50" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/75px-0050Diglett.png 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/a/a6/0050Diglett.png/100px-0050Diglett.png 2x" data-file-width="758" data-file-height="758"></a></span>
</td>
<td style="padding-left:3px; padding-right:20px"><b>This section is incomplete.</b><br>Please feel free to edit this section to add missing information and complete it. <br><small>Reason: Confirm whether the first battle's wild Pokémon can flee in Omega Ruby, Alpha Sapphire, Brilliant Diamond, and Shining Pearl</small>
</td></tr></tbody></table> 
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ruby_and_Sapphire" class="mw-redirect" title="Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire">Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Emerald_Version" title="Pokémon Emerald Version">Emerald</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Diamond_and_Pearl_Versions" title="Pokémon Diamond and Pearl Versions">Diamond and Pearl</a>, the player battles a wild Pokémon (<a href="/wiki/Poochyena_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Poochyena (Pokémon)">Poochyena</a>, <a href="/wiki/Zigzagoon_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Zigzagoon (Pokémon)">Zigzagoon</a>, or <a href="/wiki/Starly_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Starly (Pokémon)">Starly</a>) immediately after obtaining their first partner Pokémon. During this battle, if the player's Pokémon's HP bar turns red (i.e. its remaining HP is 20% or less), the wild Pokémon will flee on its turn instead of attacking.
</p><p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Sun_and_Moon" title="Pokémon Sun and Moon">Pokémon Sun, Moon</a>, <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Ultra_Sun_and_Ultra_Moon" title="Pokémon Ultra Sun and Ultra Moon">Ultra Sun, and Ultra Moon</a>, during the <a href="/wiki/Player_character" title="Player character">player</a>'s first visit to <a href="/wiki/Aether_Paradise" title="Aether Paradise">Aether Paradise</a>, there is a scripted battle against the <a href="/wiki/Ultra_Beast" title="Ultra Beast">Ultra Beast</a> <a href="/wiki/Nihilego_(Pok%C3%A9mon)" title="Nihilego (Pokémon)">Nihilego</a>. This Nihilego, which cannot be <a href="/wiki/Caught_Pok%C3%A9mon" title="Caught Pokémon">caught</a>, is scripted to flee on the fifth turn of battle, ending the battle and continuing the story. If Nihilego was unable to flee on that turn due to being trapped or in the <a href="/wiki/Semi-invulnerable_turn" title="Semi-invulnerable turn">semi-invulnerable turn</a> of <a href="/wiki/Sky_Drop_(move)" title="Sky Drop (move)">Sky Drop</a>, it will not attempt to flee on subsequent turns.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Trainers">Trainers</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Generations_I-VIII">Generations I-VIII</span></h3>
<p>Prior to <a href="/wiki/Generation_IX" title="Generation IX">Generation IX</a>, it is impossible to escape from in-game <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer" title="Pokémon Trainer">Trainer</a> battles in which Pokémon can gain <a href="/wiki/Experience" title="Experience">experience</a>.
</p><p>However, in battles against other players, attempting to escape will cause the battle to end immediately, without fail. If only one player attempts to escape, the battle ends as a loss against them, but if both players attempt to escape in the same turn, the battle ends in a draw.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Generation_IX">Generation IX</span></h3>
<p>In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Scarlet_and_Violet" title="Pokémon Scarlet and Violet">Pokémon Scarlet and Violet</a>, it is possible to escape from in-game Trainer battles. Doing so is considered a loss, thus causing the same penalties as <a href="/wiki/Black_out" title="Black out">blacking out</a>. 
In <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Legends:_Z-A" title="Pokémon Legends: Z-A">Pokémon Legends: Z-A</a>, the player can attempt to escape from <a href="/wiki/Battle_zone_(Lumiose_City)" title="Battle zone (Lumiose City)">battle zone</a> Trainers without penalty.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="In_spin-off_games">In spin-off games</span></h2>
<h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_GO"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_GO">Pokémon GO</span></h3>
<p>Wild Pokémon escaping is a key aspect of capturing in <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_GO" title="Pokémon GO">Pokémon GO</a>. Whenever the wild Pokémon breaks out of a thrown Poké Ball, there is a chance that it will run away, ending the encounter. Every species has a its own base flee rate, a flat probability of fleeing after breaking out of a Poké Ball. If the player chooses to run from a wild Pokémon encounter, the Pokémon will still remain on the overworld map until its spawn timer expires. 
</p>
<dl><dd><i>For a list of Pokémon by their base flee rates, see <a href="/wiki/List_of_Pok%C3%A9mon_by_catch_rate_in_Pok%C3%A9mon_GO" title="List of Pokémon by catch rate in Pokémon GO">List of Pokémon by catch rate in Pokémon GO</a></i></dd></dl>
<p>Pokémon encountered as <a href="/wiki/Field_Research" title="Field Research">Field</a> or <a href="/wiki/Special_Research" title="Special Research">Special Research</a> rewards will never flee. Pokémon encountered as a result of a <a href="/wiki/Raid_Battle_(GO)" title="Raid Battle (GO)">Raid Battle</a> or <a href="/wiki/Team_GO_Rocket" title="Team GO Rocket">Team GO Rocket</a> battle flee when the player runs out of <a href="/wiki/Premier_Ball" title="Premier Ball">Premier Balls</a>, but will not flee otherwise.
</p><p>Every Pokémon that spawns on the map has a timer that can range from 15 to 60 minutes. If a player is currently tracking a nearby Pokémon using the app's interface, and that Pokémon's timer expires or the player walks out of tracking range, the game will notify that the Pokémon has fled.
</p>
<div id="AdThrive_Content_4_desktop" class="adthrive-ad adthrive-content adthrive-content-4 adthrive-ad-cls" style="min-height: 250px;"></div><h3><span id="Pok.C3.A9mon_Shuffle"></span><span class="mw-headline" id="Pokémon_Shuffle">Pokémon Shuffle</span></h3>
<p>After beating a stage that is not a battle against a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trainer" title="Pokémon Trainer">Trainer</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Mega_Evolution" title="Mega Evolution">Mega-Evolved Pokémon</a> or a Pokémon that the player has already caught, the player has the chance to catch the Pokémon they fought against. The player uses a <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9_Ball_(item)" title="Poké Ball (item)">Poké Ball</a> for the first attempt to capture the Pokémon. If the Pokémon is not caught, the player gets a prompt to buy a <a href="/wiki/Great_Ball" title="Great Ball">Great Ball</a> to catch it instead. Rejecting the prompt ends the stage with the Pokémon running off screen. If the player purchases a Great Ball, they get a second chance to catch the Pokémon with the increased Catchability from the Great Ball. If this Great Ball does not catch the Pokémon, the player may purchase another Great Ball. Once again, not choosing to buy another Great Ball means the Pokémon runs away. The Pokémon has a chance to run away without the opportunity to make a purchase at any point after the first Great Ball purchase, and will run away after four Great Balls have been used. As before, this causes the stage to end. 
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="In_the_TCG">In the TCG</span></h2>
<figure class="mw-halign-right" typeof="mw:File/Thumb"><a href="/wiki/File:ImakuniDoduoEvolutions112.jpg" class="mw-file-description"><img src="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/2/26/ImakuniDoduoEvolutions112.jpg/200px-ImakuniDoduoEvolutions112.jpg" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="200" height="277" class="mw-file-element" srcset="https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/2/26/ImakuniDoduoEvolutions112.jpg/300px-ImakuniDoduoEvolutions112.jpg 1.5x, https://archives.bulbagarden.net/media/upload/thumb/2/26/ImakuniDoduoEvolutions112.jpg/400px-ImakuniDoduoEvolutions112.jpg 2x" data-file-width="600" data-file-height="832"></a><figcaption><a href="/wiki/Imakuni%3F%27s_Doduo_(Evolutions_112)" title="Imakuni?'s Doduo (Evolutions 112)">Imakuni?'s Doduo</a> has Frenzied Escape, so when it retreats it starts to run away.</figcaption></figure>
<p>As written, the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Trading_Card_Game" title="Pokémon Trading Card Game">Pokémon Trading Card Game</a> depicts a Trainer battle. As such, the concept of running away is not normally referenced directly. However, there are effects named after concepts relating to running away. For example, <i>Run Away Draw</i> on <a href="/wiki/Dudunsparce_(Temporal_Forces_129)" title="Dudunsparce (Temporal Forces 129)">Dudunsparce</a> in <a href="/wiki/Temporal_Forces_(TCG)" title="Temporal Forces (TCG)">Temporal Forces</a> is named after <a href="/wiki/Run_Away_(Ability)" title="Run Away (Ability)">Run Away</a> and <a href="/wiki/Wimpod_(Burning_Shadows_16)" title="Wimpod (Burning Shadows 16)">Wimpod</a> from <a href="/wiki/Burning_Shadows_(TCG)" title="Burning Shadows (TCG)">Burning Shadows</a> has <a href="/wiki/Wimp_Out_(Ability)" title="Wimp Out (Ability)">Wimp Out</a>. This may associate running away with the <a href="/wiki/Retreat_Cost_(TCG)" title="Retreat Cost (TCG)">retreat</a> action and with generally leaving the in-play zone.
</p><p>One card does explicitly run away: <a href="/wiki/Imakuni%3F%27s_Doduo_(Challenge_from_the_Darkness)" title="Imakuni?'s Doduo (Challenge from the Darkness)">Imakuni?'s Doduo</a>, in its original version only released in Japan in <a href="/wiki/Challenge_from_the_Darkness_(TCG)" class="mw-redirect" title="Challenge from the Darkness (TCG)">Challenge from the Darkness</a> and its <a href="/wiki/Imakuni%3F%27s_Doduo_(Evolutions_112)" title="Imakuni?'s Doduo (Evolutions 112)">updated version</a> in <a href="/wiki/Evolutions_(TCG)" title="Evolutions (TCG)">Evolutions</a>. Both cards have the <a href="/wiki/Pok%C3%A9mon_Power_(TCG)" title="Pokémon Power (TCG)">Pokémon Power</a> <i>Frenzied Escape</i>. When Imakuni?'s Doduo retreats, the player is to throw it as far as they can "because Doduo is running away". This effect means Imakuni?'s Doduo does not go to the <a href="/wiki/Bench" class="mw-redirect" title="Bench">Bench</a> after retreating like other cards. Instead, the Pokémon remains out of play for the rest of the game.
</p>
